# VHDL 2008 Grammar and Static Semantic Test Plan

**Document Version**: V2.0
**Date**: 2026-08-28
**Standard**: IEEE Std 1076-2008
**Compliance**: IEEE 829 Test Plan

---

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose

This document defines the complete test plan for validating VHDL 2008 grammar (syntax) and compile/elaboration-stage static semantic rules. The test suite ensures 100% coverage of all BNF productions defined in Annex C of IEEE Std 1076-2008 and comprehensive coverage of high-frequency static semantic constraints.

This document defines the complete test plan for validating VHDL 2008 grammar (the syntax layer) and the static semantic rules at the compile/elaboration stage. The test suite ensures 100% coverage of all BNF productions defined in Annex C of IEEE Std 1076-2008 and comprehensive coverage of high-frequency core static semantic constraints.

### 1.2 Scope

**Included**:
- All 310 BNF productions from Annex C (Syntax Summary)
- 139 core static semantic rules detectable at compile/elaboration time
- 37 VHDL predefined attributes with per-attribute test suites
- Both positive (compilable) and negative (error-triggering) test cases

**Excluded**:
- PSL assertions (PSL_Clock_Declaration, PSL_Property_Declaration, PSL_Sequence_Declaration, PSL_PSL_Directive)
- Fixed-point and floating-point packages (IEEE 1076-2008 package bodies)
- VHPI (VHDL Procedural Interface)
- VITAL (ASIC modeling extensions)
- Vendor-specific language extensions
- **All runtime semantic behaviors**: simulation timing, delta delays, execution order, event scheduling, signal resolution at runtime

### 1.3 Test Objectives

1. Verify that each BNF production is correctly recognized by a VHDL 2008-compliant parser
2. Verify that single violations of BNF productions are correctly detected
3. Verify that static semantic constraints are enforced at compile/elaboration
4. Provide full traceability from test cases back to standard clauses

---

## 2. Test Strategy

### 2.1 Test Case Design Methodology

#### Syntax Testing

| Aspect | Positive (SYN, QSYN) | Negative (SNN, QSNN) |
|---|---|---|
| Count per BNF rule | 3-5 (basic) + 4 (quality) | 2-3 (basic) + 3 (quality) |
| Design | Complete VHDL unit with complex custom types (integer/enum/array/record subtypes) | Syntactically invalid but only one rule violated |
| Expected result | Compiles successfully | Triggers specific syntax error |

#### Semantic Testing

| Aspect | Positive (SEM) | Negative (SMN) |
|---|---|---|
| Count per semantic rule | 1 | 2 |
| Design | Syntactically valid, semantically correct | Syntactically valid, semantically invalid (single rule violation) |
| Expected result | Compiles and elaborates successfully | Triggers specific semantic error |

### 2.2 Single-Rule Per Negative Case Constraint

Every negative test case must violate exactly ONE rule. This ensures error messages can be uniquely attributed to a specific rule.

Every negative test case must violate exactly one rule, and no more. This ensures that error messages can be uniquely traced back to a specific rule.

### 2.3 Test Case Naming Convention

**New chapter-based format**:
```
TC_[PRODUCTION_NAME]_[TYPE]_[NNN].vhd
```
- PRODUCTION_NAME: BNF production name, uppercase (e.g., `ARCHITECTURE_BODY`, `ENTITY_DECLARATION`)
- TYPE: `SYN` (syntax positive), `SNN` (syntax negative), `QSYN` (quality positive), `QSNN` (quality negative), `SEM` (semantic positive), `SMN` (semantic negative)
- Example: `TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_001.vhd`, `TC_ENTITY_DECLARATION_QSYN_001.vhd`

**Legacy format (syntax/semantic/attributes directories)**:
```
TC_[MODULE]_[TYPE]_[NNN].vhd
```
- MODULE: 3-letter abbreviation (DU, LEX, TYPE, DECL, SUBP, ENT, SEQ, CONC, CFG)
- Example: `TC_TYPE_SYN_001.vhd`, `TC_DECL_SMN_001.vhd`

## 3. Test Suite Architecture

### 3.1 Primary Organization: IEEE Chapter Structure

The test suite is organized by IEEE 1076-2008 chapter, with each BNF production as a subfolder.

```
cases_src/
├── ch03_design_entities/  20f, 413 files,  SYN=167 SNN=129 SEM=17 SMN=74 (specific=20)
├── ch04_subprograms_packages/  21f, 319 files,  SYN=195 SNN=79 SEM=0 SMN=16 (specific=21)
├── ch05_types/  50f, 779 files,  SYN=277 SNN=226 SEM=74 SMN=111 (specific=50)
├── ch06_declarations/  58f, 880 files,  SYN=525 SNN=202 SEM=6 SMN=55 (specific=58)
├── ch07_configuration/  19f, 315 files,  SYN=149 SNN=101 SEM=25 SMN=21 (specific=19)
├── ch08_names/  19f, 247 files,  SYN=114 SNN=79 SEM=18 SMN=14 (specific=19)
├── ch09_expressions/  32f, 557 files,  SYN=275 SNN=168 SEM=35 SMN=57 (specific=16)
├── ch10_sequential/  55f, 823 files,  SYN=362 SNN=241 SEM=28 SMN=146 (specific=28)
├── ch11_concurrent/  23f, 364 files,  SYN=137 SNN=105 SEM=31 SMN=62 (specific=22)
├── ch12_scope/  1f, 17 files,  SYN=8 SNN=5 SEM=1 SMN=2 (specific=1)
├── ch13_design_units/  8f, 129 files,  SYN=56 SNN=40 SEM=8 SMN=16 (specific=8)
├── ch15_lexical/  22f, 342 files,  SYN=120 SNN=108 SEM=0 SMN=88 (specific=22)
│
│   Each folder: SYN + SNN + SEM + SMN (generic + production-specific)
└── Grand total: 5,185 files, 328 production folders
```

### 3.2 Per-Production Folder Structure

Each production folder contains all test types colocated:
- **SYN files** (3-5):  basic positive tests with rich type declarations
- **QSYN files** (4):    quality positive tests — comprehensive with all type categories
- **SNN files** (2-3):   basic negative tests — production-specific syntax errors
- **QSNN files** (3):    quality negative tests — single-rule violation
- **SEM files** (1-3):   semantic positive tests — respects the semantic constraint
- **SMN files** (2-3):   semantic negative tests — violates exactly one semantic rule

### 3.3 File Quality Tiers

| Tier | Prefix | Content | Avg Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quality | `QSYN`, `QSNN` | Rich VHDL: custom int/enum/array/record types, state machines, clock generators, for-generate, blocks, assertions | ~3,000B |
| Basic | `SYN`, `SNN` | Complete compilable unit with essential type declarations | ~1,000B |
| Semantic | `SEM`, `SMN` | Syntactically valid VHDL with semantic correctness/violation | ~1,000B |

### 3.4 Error Category Classification

| Category | Code | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| type_mismatch | TM | 53 | Type incompatibility in assignments, expressions, associations |
| declaration_elaboration_error | DEE | 34 | Duplicate declarations, missing bodies, elaboration failures |
| scope_visibility_error | SVE | 30 | Undeclared identifiers, invisible names, invalid references |
| interface_violation | IV | 16 | Port mode violations, parameter mismatches, generic errors |
| assignment_driver_violation | ADV | 6 | Invalid targets, driver restrictions |

## 4. Test Environment

### 4.1 Tools

- **Reference VHDL 2008 Simulators**: GHDL (open-source), ModelSim/QuestaSim, Riviera-PRO
- **Test Case Management**: CSV-based metadata (`test_cases_meta.csv`, `rule_case_mapping.csv`)
- **Traceability**: Auto-generated Appendix E with 2,243 test point → file mappings

### 4.2 Test Data

All test cases are self-contained VHDL design files. No external data files, simulation models, or vendor libraries required. Each file is a complete compilable unit (entity + architecture or package declaration + body).

All test cases are self-contained VHDL design files, requiring no external dependencies.

## 7. Risk Assessment

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Batch-generated files lack specificity | Medium | Medium | Quality enhancer added rich type context to 2,170 files; hand-crafted key productions |
| Negative cases not production-specific | Low | Medium | QSNN files target specific keyword/operator errors per production |
| Complex type coverage inconsistent | Low | Low | All QSYN files use uniform rich type scaffold (custom int/enum/array/record) |
| Encoding issues in reports | Low | Low | UTF-8 with BOM for CSV; UTF-8 for markdown |

| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_004.vhd | Multiple processes coexisting: clock process (clk sensitivity) + reset process (rst_n sensitivity) + combinational process (a,b sensitivity) + wait-based process, verifying architecture_statement_part can contain any number of process concurrent statements in any style |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_005.vhd | generates: for-generate, if-generate-else, nested generate, component inst with generic+port map |

| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_007.vhd | same entity dual architectures: structural vs behavioral style |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_008.vhd | concurrent: postponed assertion, immediate assertion, concurrent signal assignment |

| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_010.vhd | comprehensive: all declarative items + all concurrent statements combined |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_011.vhd | Unconstrained port + generic combination: entity uses an unconstrained array port and a generic to control size, the declarative part derives the index range from the generic value, for-generate iterates the generic parameter, verifying full architecture support for generics and unconstrained ports |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_012.vhd | Multi-level configuration binding: architecture declarative part contains component declaration + configuration specification (for...use entity...port map) and instantiates that component, verifying architecture_declarative_part can contain a configuration specification whose binding takes effect at architecture instantiation |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_013.vhd | Guarded signal disconnect specification: declarative part contains a disconnect specification defining post-disconnection behavior for a guarded signal, a guarded block uses guarded assignment to that signal, verifying architecture_declarative_part can contain disconnect_specification and interact correctly with the guarded block |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_014.vhd | Group declarations: declarative part contains a group_template_declaration (defining the allowed entity class combinations) and a group_declaration (using that template to group signals into a named group), verifying architecture_declarative_part supports the complete group construct (VHDL 2008 group feature) |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_015.vhd | VHDL 2008 external names: an architecture process uses the <<signal external pathname : type>> syntax to reference a hierarchical external signal, verifying the statement part of the architecture can use external_name for cross-level signal access (VHDL 2008 hierarchical reference) |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_016.vhd | Minimal end form: empty declarative part + empty statement part, after end neither the "architecture" keyword nor the architecture name identifier is written, just `end;` — verifying both optional clauses `[ architecture ] [ architecture_simple_name ]` in the BNF can be omitted at the same time |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_017.vhd | Architecture containing only passive concurrent procedure calls: statement part consists of 2 concurrent_procedure_call_statements (both passive procedures, driving no signals), verifying entity_statement and architecture_statement_part allow passive concurrent procedure calls as the only concurrent statement form |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_018.vhd | All block header combinations: 4 blocks use (no header), (generic only), (port only), and (generic+port combined) respectively, verifying all 4 combinations of the block_statement block_header compile in the architecture statement part |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_019.vhd | Large-scale multi-component instantiation: declarative part declares 2 component kinds (flip-flop + inverter), for-generate batch-instantiates 8 flip-flops + 8 inverters forming a shift chain, verifying the architecture can contain many component_instantiations and for-generate can iterate multiple components |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_020.vhd | File declarations and operations: declarative part contains a file type definition (file of integer) and a file object declaration (with open_read_mode/file_logical_name), the statement part uses the file type through a subprogram, verifying architecture_declarative_part supports file_declaration and file_type_definition |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_021.vhd | Access types and allocators: declarative part contains an access type (pointer to a record) and an allocator (new expression), a process uses the access object to store and read data, verifying architecture_declarative_part supports access_type_definition and allocator expressions |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_022.vhd | All alias categories: declarative part contains an object alias (signal alias with subtype_indication), a subprogram alias (function alias with signature), and an enumeration literal alias, the statement part drives the same signal through the original name and the alias, verifying all three forms of alias_declaration are legal in architecture_declarative_part |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_023.vhd | Mixed VHDL 2008 features: declarative part contains protected type declaration + body + shared variable and an impure function, statement part contains a matching case? statement (VHDL 2008), verifying the architecture can mix multiple VHDL 2008 new syntax elements (protected type, shared var, case? matching statement) |

**Category**: Category C (structures/containers) | **Total files**: 17

#### SYN — Positive syntax tests (9 files)

| File | How to Test |
|---|---|
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_DECLARATIVE_PART_SYN_001.vhd | Empty declarative part - zero block_declarative_items: architecture goes directly to begin followed by statements, verifying { } meaning zero repetitions is legal, the most common architecture form |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_DECLARATIVE_PART_SYN_002.vhd | Type + subtype declarations: declarative part contains integer type (t_data 0..1023)/enum type (t_state IDLE,RUN,DONE)/array type 1D+2D/record type (t_pkt)/physical type (t_freq Hz/kHz)/floating type (t_gain)/subtypes (t_byte integer/t_nibble bit_vector), verifying all type_declaration+subtype_declaration categories can coexist in the architecture declarative part |
| TC_ARCHITECTURE_DECLARATIVE_PART_SYN_003.vhd | Signal + constant + file + shared variable declarations: declarative part contains signal (with register kind + default value aggregate)/constant (integer+time+bit_vector)/file type + file declaration/shared variable (with protected type), verifying all object declaration categories: signal/constant/file/shared_variable |

| TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SNN_004.vhd | SNN: port clause appears before generic clause in entity_header—`port(x:in bit); generic(G:integer:=1);` reverses the BNF order which requires `[generic_clause]` before `[port_clause]`; the parser expects optional generic clause first, so encountering the `port` keyword when `generic` is still expected triggers a syntax error at the `port` token |
| TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SNN_005.vhd | SNN: missing semicolon between generic clause and port clause—`generic(G:integer:=1) port(x:in bit)` omits the required semicolon terminator after the generic clause's closing parenthesis; the BNF production defines two distinct optional clauses and a semicolon is required to separate them, so the parser encountering `port` immediately after `)` without an intervening `;` reports a missing semicolon error |
| TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SNN_006.vhd | SNN: missing closing parenthesis in the formal_generic_clause—`generic(G:integer:=1; H:boolean` opens the generic clause with `(` but never closes it with `)`, so the parser encounters `port` while still inside the unclosed generic clause parenthesized scope; the error manifests as an unexpected `port` token where `)` or another generic declaration was expected, validating that the optional generic clause requires balanced parentheses |
| TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SNN_007.vhd | SNN: missing closing parenthesis in the formal_port_clause—`port(a:in bit; b:out integer` opens the port clause with `(` but never closes it, so the parser reaches `end entity` while still inside the unclosed port clause parenthesized scope; the BNF requires that every `(` in a port_clause has a matching `)`, and the missing closer causes the entity declaration to be malformed because the parser cannot find the port clause terminator |

#### SEM/SMN — Semantic tests (5 files)

| Rule | File | How to Test |
|---|---|---|
| BNF_ENTITY_HEADER | TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SMN_001.vhd | SMN: port subtype_indication references an undeclared generic name—`generic(G_W:integer:=8); port(din:in bit_vector(WIDTH-1 downto 0))` refers to `WIDTH` in the port constraint, but the generic clause only declares `G_W`; the identifier `WIDTH` is not visible in the entity header scope, so the semantic analyzer must reject the port's subtype_indication for referencing an undeclared name within the same entity_header declarative region |
| BNF_ENTITY_HEADER | TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SMN_002.vhd | SMN: generic clause declares a type interface with an unconstrained array but no index constraint resolution—`generic(type vec_t is array(integer range <>) of bit); port(v:in vec_t)` uses an unconstrained array generic type for a port in `in` mode; in VHDL 2008, port `in` mode signals of an unconstrained generic array type require the actual to provide the index constraint at elaboration, but the semantic analyzer must verify that the entity_header itself is syntactically well-formed with an unconstrained generic type used in a port declaration, which is legal in VHDL 2008 and serves as a boundary case that exercises the full generic type interface capability within entity_header |
| BNF_ENTITY_HEADER | TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SMN_003.vhd | SEM: generic identifier and port identifier collide within entity_header—`generic(DATA:integer:=8); port(DATA:in bit_vector(7 downto 0))` declares the same name `DATA` as both a generic constant and a port signal; although both declarations are syntactically correct per their respective BNF sub-productions, the entity header forms a single declarative region and VHDL prohibits name collisions between generics and ports within the same entity |
| BNF_ENTITY_HEADER | TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SMN_2.vhd | SEM: duplicate generic identifier in formal_generic_clause—`generic(G_W:integer:=8; G_W:boolean:=true)` declares the same identifier `G_W` twice within the generic clause; although the BNF syntax is valid (both are legal interface_constant_declarations), the VHDL scoping rules forbid duplicate declarations within the same declarative region, so the semantic analyzer must reject the duplicate `G_W` identifier in the entity header's generic list |
| BNF_ENTITY_HEADER | TC_ENTITY_HEADER_SMN_3.vhd | SEM: duplicate port identifier in formal_port_clause—`port(clk:in bit; rst:in bit; clk:out bit)` declares `clk` twice within the same port clause with different modes; while the BNF syntax for each port declaration is individually valid, the entity header's declarative region must contain unique port identifiers, so the analyzer rejects the duplicate `clk` identifier within the port list |

| Rule | File | How to Test |
|---|---|---|
| BNF_LETTER | TC_LETTER_SMN_001.vhd | SMN: Identifier starting with a digit — in signal 2bad the first character of the identifier is a digit, basic_identifier must start with letter |
| BNF_LETTER | TC_LETTER_SMN_002.vhd | SMN: Identifier starting with underscore — in signal _ab the first character of the identifier is underscore, basic_identifier must start with letter, underscore may appear only between letters or digits |
| BNF_LETTER | TC_LETTER_SMN_2.vhd | Uppercase/lowercase letters in identifiers — VHDL identifiers are case insensitive, MySig and mysig are semantically the same identifier causing duplicate declaration |
| BNF_LETTER | TC_LETTER_SMN_3.vhd | Reserved word entity used as a signal name — reserved words are made of letters but cannot be used as ordinary identifiers, semantic check should reject it |

### 9.326 letter_or_digit (Ch.15, Lexical Elements)

**Category**: Category C (structures/containers) | **Total files**: 16

#### SYN — Positive syntax tests (6 files)

| File | How to Test |
|---|---|
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SYN_001.vhd | letter branch — all characters of the identifier except the first are letters, verify letter as a subset of letter_or_digit |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SYN_002.vhd | Digits used as body characters in a basic identifier (after the first character which must be a letter) |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SYN_003.vhd | digit branch — digits embedded in identifiers as non-first character parts of letter_or_digit, such as addr1, bus32 |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SYN_004.vhd | letter and digit mixed in identifiers — underscore separators followed by digits, verify the alternating use of the two forms of letter_or_digit |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SYN_005.vhd | letter and digit used in extended_identifier — identifiers inside \...\ can use any letter_or_digit for non-first characters |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SYN_006.vhd | DSP-style identifiers — stage numbers, channel numbers and width suffixes using digits, comprehensively test complex combinations of letter_or_digit in real RTL |

#### SNN — Negative syntax tests (5 files)

| File | How to Test |
|---|---|
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SNN_001.vhd | Identifier containing the special character # — # is neither a letter nor a digit, violating the letter_or_digit definition |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SNN_002.vhd | Invalid character '@' in an identifier body — letter_or_digit must be letter or digit, '@' is neither |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SNN_003.vhd | letter_or_digit: type mismatch in declaration |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SNN_004.vhd | Identifier containing a space as a separator — space is not letter_or_digit, its appearance inside an identifier causes token splitting |
| TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SNN_005.vhd | SNN: identifier ending with a trailing underscore — in signal ab_ there is no letter_or_digit after the underscore, basic_identifier cannot end with an underscore |

#### SEM/SMN — Semantic tests (4 files)

| Rule | File | How to Test |
|---|---|---|
| BNF_LETTER_OR_DIGIT | TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SMN_001.vhd | Trailing underscore leaves letter_or_digit missing — underscore must be followed by letter_or_digit, it cannot end an identifier |
| BNF_LETTER_OR_DIGIT | TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SMN_002.vhd | Identifier confused with a reserved word through case — END is a reserved word but end is formed from letter_or_digit with the exact same name, semantic check should reject it |
| BNF_LETTER_OR_DIGIT | TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SMN_2.vhd | Identifier starting with a digit — the first character must be letter (not letter_or_digit), digits may only be used in non-first positions |
| BNF_LETTER_OR_DIGIT | TC_LETTER_OR_DIGIT_SMN_3.vhd | SEM: Two consecutive underscores in an identifier — in signal a__b there is no letter_or_digit between the underscores, in basic_identifier underscore may only separate letters or digits |

### 9.327 string_literal (Ch.15, Lexical Elements)

**Category**: Category E (lexical) | **Total files**: 16

#### SYN — Positive syntax tests (6 files)

| File | How to Test |
|---|---|
| TC_STRING_LITERAL_SYN_001.vhd | String literal multiple use scenarios: string constant assignment (with spaces)/bit_vector assignment/attribute values/report messages, verify the use of printable character sequences of string_literal in different contexts |

| TC_STRING_LITERAL_SYN_004.vhd | String containing escaped double quotes — two consecutive double quotes in a string denote one literal double quote character, test the boundary case of graphic_character |
| TC_STRING_LITERAL_SYN_005.vhd | Long string containing spaces and punctuation — graphic_character can include space, comma, period etc., test common printable characters in strings |

## Appendix C: File Header Template

Every VHDL test case file must begin with the following standard header:

```vhdl
-- =============================================================
-- Case ID: [case_id]
-- Rule Type: [Syntax / Semantic]
-- Related Rule ID: [bnf_id or semantic rule_id]
-- Standard Reference: IEEE 1076-2008 Section [X.Y.Z]
-- Production: [BNF rule text]
-- Case Type: [Positive / Negative]
-- Test Focus: [specific test point description]
-- Expected Result: [Compiles successfully / Triggers X error]
-- Dependencies: [None / required package files]
-- =============================================================
```
